{{Quote|I also acknowledge the Council's observation that the Force runs strong in my family. My uncle was a Jedi Knight, as is my niece Sha Koon.|Plo Koon, recording in the Great Holocron|<ref name="JvS" />}}
A [[Kel Dor/Legends|Kel Dor]] '''member''' of the [[Koon family]] was [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]], serving as a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Knight]] in the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. They were an [[Gender/Legends|uncle]] of the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]] and was also related to Koon's niece [[Sha Koon]]. In a recording made in the [[Great Holocron/Legends|Great Holocron]] by Plo Koon after an incident where he used the [[Electric Judgment|light side application]] of [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] acknowledged his bloodline's sensitivity to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and the Kel Dor reputation for perceiving issues of morality in [[Color/Legends|black]] and white. Since he assumed responsibility for his own actions, Plo Koon asked the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] to disregard his uncle and niece's presence in the Order in their judgement.<ref name="JvS" /> In [[30 BBY/Legends|30 BBY]], Koon mentioned his uncle as he related the events of the [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]] to the [[Amnesia/Legends|amnesiac]] Jedi [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]].<ref name="SHW">[[Star Wars (1998) 39|''Star Wars'' (1998) 39]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Plo Koon's uncle was first mentioned in the [[Star Wars (1998) 39|thirty-ninth issue]] of the [[1998]] [[Star Wars: Republic|''Star Wars'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic-book]] series. The issue was written by [[John Ostrander]] and published by [[Dark Horse Comics]]<ref name="SHW" /> on [[February 20]], [[2002]].<ref name="Date">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/53934/star_wars_1998_39|text=Star Wars (1998) #39}}</ref>
